key_insight: Water adsorption and especially H2O dissociation on g-C3N4 nanosheets can boost optical absorbance and electrical conductance, improving their promise for photocatalytic water splitting.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests g-C3N4 is a viable low-cost photocatalyst candidate whose performance can be tuned by controlling surface water chemistry for hydrogen production systems.
method: DFT used to benchmark the pristine and adsorbed nanosheet electronic/optical structure
SCC-DFTB simulations extended the atomistic analysis for OH and H2O adsorption effects
ReaxFF molecular dynamics modeled multi-H2O emission and linked dissociation behavior to H2 evolution rate
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that dissociation of H2O into HO and O significantly increased absorbance and conductance relative to pristine g-C3N4, supporting improved photocatalytic behavior.
watch_item: The conclusions come from computational models, so experimental validation is still needed to confirm stability, reaction pathways, and real-device performance.
paper_title: Computational Study of Water Adsorption and Dissociative Mechanisms Impacting g-C3N4's Optical and Electronic Properties
